title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android: Town Hall front-of-room view control (Worldwide)
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents what presenter view displays, so the briefing incorrectly treats that information as unavailable. The roadmap facts, Teams Rooms Pro requirement, attendee-view default and events-policy controls are supported.

claims.quote: When a Teams Rooms on Android is invited as a meeting presenter, the front-of-room display defaults to the attendee view.

claims.quote: If you’re in an MTR where both presenters and attendees are present, switch to **Attendee view** to hide the presenter controls on the front display.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter and cost
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap item nor the release notes name a meter for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams Rooms" "front-of-room view control" "price" "meter"; opened roadmap record, rooms-release-note and rooms-licensing. These identify Teams Rooms Pro but no meter for this display-view feature.

claims.claim: The setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote:
go to **Meetings** > **Events policies**.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
turn the **Events optimized for a large audience** toggle **On** or **Off**.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled disables creation of events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote:
### -AllowTownhalls
**Disabled**: Disables the **Optimize for Large Audience** option for organizers scheduling an event.
### -Identity
Unique identifier assigned to the Teams Events policy.

claims.claim: The events policy is user-scoped.
claims.quote: User-level policy for tenant admin to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences.

claims.claim: Events optimized for a large audience governs whether users with the policy can create events such as Town Halls.
claims.quote: Controls whether users with this policy can create events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls.

claims.claim: Changing the events setting to Off after an event is scheduled prevents the user running or starting it.
claims.quote: If you change the value to **Off** after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference describes the events policy as still in preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows you to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described what presenter view shows on the front-of-room display.
claims.quote: It will also show the **Manage screen** queue where presenters are brought on and off screen, as well as a red square around the live feed to indicate what attendees are currently seeing.
claims.fix: Remove ', because the sources do not describe its contents' from the Data exposure bullet and remove the Open questions bullet beginning 'What does presenter view show'. Microsoft describes the display contents under 'Presenter and attendee views' at https://support.microsoft.com/office/host-or-attend-an-event-from-a-microsoft-teams-room-mtr-d7ff15e0-6516-4ebc-ae03-a2bdf58a4478, linked from the Android release notes.
